Subject: Polestar POC: realtime assistant SLA/throughput questions

Nikhil,

Thanks for taking this call earlier. We're starting the engineering kickoff for the realtime assistant POC and need to size Dedicated capacity for an expected pilot workload:~
- Peak transactional QPS: 250 requests/sec (each request ~ 60 prompt tokens, expecting ~120 tokens generated)
- Expected traffic shape: diurnal with two short spikes, but worst-case sustained hour-long peaks
- SLO: p95 inference latency < 300ms (end-to-end token-return), p99 < 700ms

Two quick asks:
1) What Dedicated pool sizing do you recommend to meet the SLO with reasonable headroom (30-50%)?
2) What assumptions are you using for tokens/sec per GPU and for KV/prefix cache impact?

Attached a small spreadsheet with our QPS assumptions. Also looping in Raj (infra lead).

From: nikhil_sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Polestar POC: realtime assistant SLA/throughput questions

Emma — thanks for the details and the sheet. Quick summary below; I put the worked numbers into throughput_calc.csv and attached it for review.

High-level assumptions (baseline):
- Target generation per request: 120 tokens average
- Prompt tokens per request: 60 tokens
- Total tokens per request = 180 tokens
- Peak RPS = 250 requests/sec => peak tokens/sec = 250 * 180 = 45,000 tokens/sec

Model variants we recommend testing (tradeoffs):
A) Open-7B-quant (fast variant): ~18k-25k tokens/sec per A100-80GB GPU depending on batch shape and quantization. Typical p95 single-token latency ~120-180ms for streaming (low-latency mode).
B) Open-13B-quant (balanced): ~10k-15k tokens/sec per A100, p95 ~180-300ms.
C) Open-70B-quant (high-quality): ~2.5k-4k tokens/sec per A100 (or better on H100), p95 often >400ms without aggressive batching.

Sizing logic:
- For the 7B path (A): tokens/sec per GPU = 22,000 (we used a conservative working number).
- Required GPUs (raw) = ceil(45,000 / 22,000) = 3 GPUs => with 30% headroom => 4 GPUs.
- For the 13B path: tokens/sec per GPU = 12,000 => raw = 4 => with 40% headroom => 6 GPUs.
- For the 70B path (if you want production-grade quality): tokens/sec per GPU = 3,000 => raw = 15 => with 50% headroom => 23 GPUs (H100 recommended).

Important notes on latency and headroom: we size for steady-state token throughput, but p95 latency is heavily affected by concurrency, batching window, and KV/prefix cache hit-rate. Example impact:
- With a 60% KV cache hit-rate (prefix reuse), effective GPU tokens/sec demand drops ~30-40% because prefix KV avoids recomputing early layers for repeated context.
- If you enable continuous batching for short-lived requests, you can increase GPU utilization but it adds tail-latency pressure — we tune batching window to hit p95 targets.

Recommended Dedicated configuration for POC (practical):
- Start: 4x A100-80GB (7B quant path) with autoscale policy to add 2 more GPUs on sustained >15% utilization for >10m. This gives expected p95 < 250ms under the modeled traffic and ~30-40% headroom for short spikes.
- Canary: Run a 48h stress with synthetic traffic that reproduces 1.5x peak for 30m windows to validate tail latencies.
- Fallback: Provision 2x smaller-variant replicas for degraded-quality fast-path (if quality drop acceptable).

I'll capture these in the Deal page and produce a short runbook for the 48h test. Attaching throughput_calc.csv (calcs + sensitivity).

Cheers,
Nikhil Sharma
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

Thanks — a few clarifying Qs before we lock the trial commit. Quoting Nikhil below: 

> For the 7B path (A): tokens/sec per GPU = 22,000 (we used a conservative working number).
> Required GPUs (raw) = ceil(45,000 / 22,000) = 3 GPUs => with 30% headroom => 4 GPUs.

1) Could you share the microbench that produced 22k tokens/sec (batch size, seq len, model repo)? We need to validate that number against our own internal benchmark (we run a customized tokenizer and have slightly different average token lengths).
2) How sensitive is the 30% headroom to KV cache hit-rate? If we achieve 70% prefix reuse, can we drop to 3 GPUs for the 7B path and keep p95 < 300ms?
3) For the fallback replicas you mention — what policy do you use for automatic model fallback (latency-based vs capacity-based)?

Requested next steps: please attach the throughput_calc.csv and the microbench command/params so Raj can run a quick local check. Also — can Redwood run the 48h synthetic spike from your side so we can monitor observability traces and confirm p95 under load?

Appreciate it — Raj
